readings: Join riskandmargin to orders (ordervault = recordvault) and orders to users (userlink = userstamp), dropping unmatched rows. For each users.acctscope, count the joined rows, so an order with several risk/margin records is counted once per record. Show the scope, that count, its share of the total count across all scopes, and the count divided by the average count per scope (averaged over the scopes that appear), all unrounded.

Join riskandmargin to orders (ordervault = recordvault) and orders to users (userlink = userstamp), dropping unmatched rows. For each users.acctscope, count the DISTINCT orders (distinct orders.recordvault) that have at least one matching risk/margin record, so an order with several risk/margin records is counted once. Show the scope, that distinct-order count, its share of the total distinct-order count across all scopes, and the count divided by the average distinct-order count per scope (averaged over the scopes that appear), all unrounded.
queries:
SELECT acctscope,
       cnt,
       cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share,
       cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg
FROM (
  SELECT u.acctscope AS acctscope, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM riskandmargin r
  JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY u.acctscope
);
WITH scope_counts AS (
  SELECT u.acctscope AS acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count
  FROM riskandmargin r
  JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY u.acctscope
)
SELECT
  acctscope,
  order_count,
  order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total,
  order_count * 1.0 / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg
FROM scope_counts;
